body.name: Inductive exact shared-trace extension
body.construction:
Fix a safe-sector system produced by \(\mathrm{lem:computable\mbox{-}safe\mbox{-}recession\mbox{-}sectors}\) and put \(q_s=K*\phi_{s^2\Sigma}\).  For a sector \(\alpha\), decompose the whitened Gaussian coordinate into the \(\Sigma^{-1}\)-orthogonal spaces \(N_\alpha\oplus T_\alpha\), let \(Z_\alpha\) be the centered residual tangential Gaussian, and let \(H_{\alpha,L}\) be a rational box contained in the safe cone \(C_\alpha\).  Define the cone-interior candidate on the bounded normal base by
\[
 q_\alpha^\circ(n,A)=\frac{1}{|H_{\alpha,L}|}
 \int_{H_{\alpha,L}}E\!left[
 q_s\{\varsigma_\alpha(n)+t+Z_\alpha,A\}\right]dt,
 \qquad A\in\mathcal A.
\]
The box integral is the product of the literally shared one-ray averaging factors on every incident cone.  On the barycentric subdivision, construct \(\widehat q\) by induction in stratum dimension.  An already constructed lower-skeleton rule is extended constantly through the new normal collar; it is used unchanged on every branching intersection.  In the part of an incident cone belonging only to that cone, interpolate convexly between this extension and \(q_\alpha^\circ\) with rational piecewise-linear cutoffs whose Mahalanobis dual derivative is at most \(L^{-1}\).  Distinct collars are separated by a rational guard width \(B\).  A single global rational simplicial mesh is used on all bounded normal bases, and a vertex on a common face is one shared action-probability variable.  Thus every chart is the restriction of the same global Markov kernel \(\widehat q\), while the cone-interior candidate retains the common-ray F\o lner representation.
inputs: a safe-sector certificate and one ancestor \(q_s=K*\phi_{s^2\Sigma}\)
rational smoothing, collar, guard, mesh, and quantization scales
